text: Git branching is a core part of version control, especially when working on a team. Instead of making all changes directly on the main codebase, developers create feature branches. These are separate copies of the project where you can add new features, fix bugs, or experiment safely. Once your work is complete and tested, you can merge it back into the main branch. However, before merging, many teams use pull requests. A pull request is a request to review and approve your changes before they become part of the final version. This workflow keeps the main code stable, encourages collaboration, and makes it easy to track who changed what and why.
